title: 森林之歌 = FOREST CHINA | Sen lin zhi ge = FOREST CHINA
summary: Forest China is nature documentary. It is a major production that has taken China Central Television (CCTV) four years to complete. It covers most of China's major forest. They are the vast forests in the Northeast of China, Qinling mountains, the Taklamakan Desert, the primitive forest of Southeastern Tibet, Shennongjia Mountains in Hubei Province, the Hengduan Mountains, the tropical rain forest in Hainan and mangroves of the South China Sea. The documentary features such rare trees as red birches, diversiform-leaved poplars, Chinese silver firs, ginkgos and seed berarer trees. It also show some of China's unique animal species, such as the panda, the golden monkey, takin, nippoina, the Northeast China tiger and gibbon. It also covers the people who live in forests, their lifestyle and their culture. Forest China is remarkable result of meticulours research and planning. It showcase China's latest effort in protecting the nature and preserving the ecology in the country. It is fact the only visual document of modern China's flora and fauna.

title: Museum Collections Management
author: Matassa, Freda
summary: "Collections Management is a relatively new term in museums, and yet it is fundamental to what museums do and why they exist. To collect, display, care for and access museum objects, was and remains the core purpose of our museums and galleries. Recently the term has come to be synonymous with database systems to store and generate information on collections, but in its wider sense, it encompasses all the activities of those engaged in caring for our national heritage. The purpose of this book is to answer all questions from what is collections management and why it is important, to how to classify objects or draw up a contract for a shared acquisition. As such, this is the first publication of its kind to act as a comprehensive and practical guide to collections management."--Publisher
